## Evaluation contract

`benchmark_spatial_refiners()` evaluates each method on identical inputs and the
same reference data:

- coordinates (`xy`)
- initial labels (`labels`)
- optional specimen ids (`samples`)
- optional boundary/sparse annotations used for stratified scores

It reports elapsed time and a standard metric table generated by
`evaluate_spatial_refinement()`.

### Standard metrics reported

- `accuracy`, `initial_accuracy`, `accuracy_gain`
- `correction_recall` and `damage_rate`
- `worst_recall`, `macro_recall`
- `boundary_accuracy`, `sparse_region_accuracy`
- `ari`

## Benchmark data

The benchmark inputs below are either bundled with the R package or
obtained directly from their original distributors. For the study's fixed
case manifests, exact corruption seeds, checksums and preparation scripts,
use the companion benchmark archive (Supplementary data 2). Run its
preparation and replay commands from the extracted archive. Follow the
upstream access and attribution terms for each external input.

### Bundled CRC and DLPFC inputs

Release 0.2 contains coordinate-and-label derivatives for colorectal
cancer (CRC) Visium HD and human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)
Visium. The package does not include the original expression counts or
images. To download and install the release used to replay the benchmarks,
run the following in R (a C++17 toolchain is required for a source install):

```{r install-benchmark-release, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("Rcpp", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("Rcpp")
tarball <- tempfile(fileext = ".tar.gz")
release <- paste0(
  "https://github.com/tkcaccia/fibermargin/releases/download/",
  "v0.2/fibermargin_0.2.tar.gz"
)
download.file(release, tarball, mode = "wb")
install.packages(tarball, repos = NULL, type = "source")
unlink(tarball)
```

Start a fresh R session after installing over a loaded version. Use
`available_spatial_benchmarks()` to see the source, redistribution terms,
and case counts:

```{r scenarios}
library(fibermargin)
available_spatial_benchmarks()
```

```{r load}
dlpfc <- load_spatial_benchmark("dlpfc", scenario = 1L)
names(dlpfc)
```

```{r load-crc, eval=FALSE}
crc <- load_spatial_benchmark("crc", "CRC_random_25_r1", seed = 1040001L)
```

Use the archive's case manifests for exact replays of all published
conditions. Original study inputs are available from
[10x Genomics (CRC)](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/visium-hd-cytassist-gene-expression-libraries-of-human-crc-v4)
and [spatialLIBD (DLPFC)](https://research.libd.org/spatialLIBD/).

### Mouse hypothalamus (MERFISH)

The original multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization
(MERFISH) study data are at [Dryad](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.8t8s248).
The benchmark uses five planes from animal 1 with labels derived from
the [BASS analysis](https://zhengli09.github.io/BASS-Analysis/MERFISH.html),
not the raw molecule table. Download the exact processed input used in the
replay from its existing upstream repository:

```sh
mkdir -p data-raw/external
merfish_rev=93ae0ce63fa3a055194c102bb143dd602d55302b
curl -fL --retry 2 -o data-raw/external/MERFISH-input.RData \
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkcaccia/KODAMA-Analysis/${merfish_rev}/data/MERFISH-input.RData"
Rscript scripts/prepare_merfish_replay.R \
  data-raw/external/MERFISH-input.RData rerun/merfish-inputs
```

The preparation script verifies the file's SHA-256 checksum before reading
it and writes the replay inputs to `rerun/merfish-inputs`. It requires the
R packages `digest` and `FNN`. The processed input is not redistributed by
FiberMargin.

### CamVid

Obtain the Cambridge-driving Labeled Video Database (CamVid) files at the
recorded revision of the [SegNet tutorial](https://github.com/alexgkendall/SegNet-Tutorial):

```sh
mkdir -p data-raw/external
camvid_dir=data-raw/external/SegNet-Tutorial
camvid_rev=bb68b64e72cb004b3ed927fee0f5624dd8097498
git init "$camvid_dir"
git -C "$camvid_dir" fetch --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/alexgkendall/SegNet-Tutorial.git "$camvid_rev"
git -C "$camvid_dir" checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
python3 scripts/prepare_camvid_full_grid.py \
  benchmarks/prepare_real_upstream_mask_predictions.py .
```

The preparation script uses the `CamVid/train`, `trainannot`, `test` and
`testannot` directories from the upstream checkout.

### Stanford 3D Indoor Spaces (S3DIS)

Review the [S3DIS terms](https://cvg-data.inf.ethz.ch/s3dis/ReadMe.txt).
The replay uses the preprocessed HDF5 shards documented by
[PointNet](https://github.com/charlesq34/pointnet/tree/master/sem_seg), not
the original or axis-aligned scene ZIP. After obtaining
`indoor3d_sem_seg_hdf5_data.zip` under the applicable terms, extract and
prepare it as follows. PointNet's
[download script](https://github.com/charlesq34/pointnet/blob/master/sem_seg/download_data.sh)
records the original URL for that archive.

```sh
mkdir -p data-raw/external/s3dis
unzip /path/to/indoor3d_sem_seg_hdf5_data.zip -d data-raw/external/s3dis
python3 benchmarks/prepare_s3dis_upstream_predictions.py
```

### ADE20K

Download the [MIT Scene Parsing benchmark](https://github.com/CSAILVision/sceneparsing)
archive and the exact [NVIDIA SegFormer model snapshot](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512/tree/489d5cd81a0b59fab9b7ea758d3548ebe99677da).
The image archive is approximately 1 GB. The `hf` command is provided by
the `huggingface_hub` Python package.

```sh
mkdir -p data-raw/external
curl -fL --retry 2 -o data-raw/external/ADEChallengeData2016.zip \
  https://data.csail.mit.edu/places/ADEchallenge/ADEChallengeData2016.zip
hf download nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512 \
  config.json preprocessor_config.json model.safetensors \
  --revision 489d5cd81a0b59fab9b7ea758d3548ebe99677da \
  --local-dir data-raw/external/segformer-b0
python3 scripts/prepare_ade20k_segformer.py data-raw/external/segformer-b0 \
  rerun/ade20k-masks --archive data-raw/external/ADEChallengeData2016.zip
```

These commands prepare the inputs for the saved-prediction benchmarks.
CamVid, S3DIS and ADE20K predictions are not bundled. Use the environment
versions and input checksums in the companion archive when reproducing
the reported results.

## Example benchmark run

```{r one-run, eval=FALSE}
bench <- simulate_spatial_domains(
  n = 5000L,
  pattern = "jagged_stripes",
  noise = 0.20,
  samples = 2L,
  seed = 7L
)

benchmark_spatial_refiners(
  data = bench,
  methods = list(
    FiberMargin = FiberMargin,
    InitialOnly = function(xy, labels, ...) labels
  ),
  include_initial = TRUE,
  seed = 1L
)
```

## Reproducibility scripts

```sh
Rscript benchmarks/benchmark_public_api.R /tmp/fibermargin-api-benchmark
Rscript benchmarks/benchmark_release_workers.R /tmp/fibermargin-worker-benchmark
```

Run these commands from the GitHub checkout with the version of fibermargin
you want to audit installed. Each script uses fixed input seeds and writes its
results to the specified directory.
